name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  CARGO_INCREMENTAL: "0"
  RUSTC_WRAPPER: sccache
  SCCACHE_GHA_ENABLED: "true"

jobs:
  checks:
    name: Rust checks
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Set up Rust
        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: clippy, rustfmt

      - name: Set up sccache
        uses: mozilla-actions/sccache-action@v0.0.9

      - name: Check formatting
        run: cargo fmt --all -- --check

      - name: Clippy
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --locked

      - name: Build
        run: cargo build --workspace --locked

      - name: Test
        run: cargo test --workspace --locked

#
# This workflow calls the main distribution pipeline from DuckDB to build, test and (optionally) release the extension
#
name: Main Extension Distribution Pipeline
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}-${{ github.head_ref || '' }}-${{ github.base_ref || '' }}-${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' || github.sha }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  duckdb-stable-build:
    name: Build extension binaries
    uses: duckdb/extension-ci-tools/.github/workflows/_extension_distribution.yml@main
    with:
      duckdb_version: v2.0.0
      ci_tools_version: main
      extension_name: rusty_quack
      extra_toolchains: rust;python3
      exclude_archs: 'linux_amd64_musl'

[workspace]
members = ["crates/core", "crates/native", "crates/wasm"]
default-members = ["crates/native"]
resolver = "3"

[workspace.package]
version = "0.1.0"
edition = "2024"

[workspace.dependencies]
duckdb-neo = { version = "=0.20000.1", features = ["build-extension"] }
rusty_quack_core = { path = "crates/core" }

[profile.release]
lto = true
strip = true

[package]
name = "rusty_quack_wasm"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true

[lib]
name = "rusty_quack"
crate-type = ["staticlib"]

[dependencies]
duckdb-neo.workspace = true
rusty_quack_core.workspace = true

[package]
name = "rusty_quack_core"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true

[dependencies]
duckdb-neo.workspace = true

[package]
name = "rusty_quack"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true

[lib]
crate-type = ["cdylib"]

[dependencies]
duckdb-neo.workspace = true
rusty_quack_core.workspace = true

# DuckDB Rust extension template
This is an **experimental** template for Rust based extensions based on the C Extension API of DuckDB. The goal is to
turn this eventually into a stable basis for pure-Rust DuckDB extensions that can be submitted to the Community extensions
repository

Features:
- No DuckDB build required
- No C++ or C code required
- CI/CD chain preconfigured
- (Coming soon) Works with community extensions

## Cloning

Clone the repo with submodules

```shell
git clone --recurse-submodules <repo>
```

## Dependencies
In principle, these extensions can be compiled with the Rust toolchain alone. However, this template relies on some additional
tooling to make life a little easier and to be able to share CI/CD infrastructure with extension templates for other languages:

- Python3
- Python3-venv
- [Make](https://www.gnu.org/software/make)
- Git

Installing these dependencies will vary per platform:
- For Linux, these come generally pre-installed or are available through the distro-specific package manager.
- For MacOS, [homebrew](https://formulae.brew.sh/).
- For Windows, [chocolatey](https://community.chocolatey.org/).

## Project layout

The Cargo workspace contains three crates:

- `crates/core` (`rusty_quack_core`): the shared function implementations and registration.
- `crates/native` (`rusty_quack`): a native `cdylib` with the DuckDB extension entrypoint.
- `crates/wasm` (`rusty_quack_wasm`): a Wasm `staticlib` with the same entrypoint.

Both entrypoint crates depend on `rusty_quack_core`. Each feature lives in its own module under `crates/core/src/`,
and `crates/core/src/lib.rs` registers them; see [What the extension registers](#what-the-extension-registers).
Dependency versions and release settings are shared in the root `Cargo.toml`.

## Building
After installing the dependencies, building is a two-step process. Firstly run:
```shell
make configure
```
This will ensure a Python venv is set up with DuckDB and DuckDB's test runner installed. Additionally, depending on configuration,
DuckDB will be used to determine the correct platform for which you are compiling.

Then, to build the extension run:
```shell
make debug
```
This delegates the build process to cargo, which will produce a shared library in `target/debug/<shared_lib_name>`. After this step,
a script is run to transform the shared library into a loadable extension by appending a binary footer. The resulting extension is written
to the `build/debug` directory.

To create optimized release binaries, simply run `make release` instead.

### WASM

To build for WASM targets, please run `make wasm_eh`. This will create `./build/wasm_eh/release/rusty_quack.duckdb_extension.wasm`, that can then be used inside nodejs or an browser.
### Running the extension
To run the extension code, start `duckdb` with `-unsigned` flag. This will allow you to load the local extension file.

```sh
duckdb -unsigned -cmd "LOAD '$PWD/build/debug/extension/rusty_quack/rusty_quack.duckdb_extension';"
```

The extension must be loaded into the exact DuckDB version it was built for (`TARGET_DUCKDB_VERSION` in the Makefile).

### What the extension registers

The template is a small tour of what a Rust extension can register through DuckDB's C API v2. Every function is
documented, so `SELECT * FROM duckdb_functions() WHERE categories = ['rusty_quack']` lists them with descriptions and
examples.

| Module (`crates/core/src/`) | Feature of `duckdb-neo` | Try it |
|---|---|---|
| `scalar.rs` | scalar function with per-query init state | `SELECT rusty_echo('Jane')` |
| `quack.rs` | table function with bind data, global and local state | `SELECT * FROM rusty_quack(['Jane', 'Doe'])` |
| `aggregate.rs` | aggregate function: init, update, combine, finalize; order-independent | `SELECT rusty_longest(name) FROM t` |
| `sequence.rs` | chunked table function with projection and filter pushdown, cardinality and progress | `SELECT i FROM rusty_sequence(10000) WHERE i < 10` |
| `quack_type.rs` | custom type and a cast into it, with `CAST` and `TRY_CAST` semantics | `SELECT 3::QUACK, TRY_CAST(11 AS QUACK)` |

```sql
SELECT rusty_echo('Jane');
```

```
┌─────────────────────┐
│ rusty_echo('Jane')  │
│       varchar       │
├─────────────────────┤
│ 🐤 Jane 🦀 Jane     │
└─────────────────────┘
```

```sql
SELECT * FROM rusty_quack(['Jane', 'Doe', 'Loves', 'Ducks']);
```

```
┌─────────┬─────────┬───────────────────────┬─────────────┐
│  name   │  icon   │      concat_name      │ total_index │
│ varchar │ varchar │        varchar        │   uint64    │
├─────────┼─────────┼───────────────────────┼─────────────┤
│ Ducks   │ 🐤      │ Ducks|                │           0 │
│ Loves   │ 🦀      │ Ducks|Loves|          │           1 │
│ Doe     │ 🐥      │ Ducks|Loves|Doe|      │           2 │
│ Jane    │ 🐤      │ Ducks|Loves|Doe|Jane| │           3 │
└─────────┴─────────┴───────────────────────┴─────────────┘
```

`EXPLAIN` shows the optimizer hooks at work. The scan lists only the projected columns, and there is
no `Filter` node: `rusty_sequence` claimed `i < 5` in `pushdown_filter`, so DuckDB dropped its own copy
and the function enforces the filter while scanning.

```sql
EXPLAIN SELECT i FROM rusty_sequence(10000) WHERE i < 5;
```

```
╭─ Rusty Sequence ─────────╮
│ Function: RUSTY_SEQUENCE │
│ Projections: i           │
│ ~10,000 rows             │
╰──────────────────────────╯
```

The `~10,000 rows` is the cardinality that `bind` declared with `set_cardinality`; it is reported before
any filter is pushed down and cannot be revised afterwards, so it stays at the full count even though the
query returns 5 rows. A filter the function does not claim keeps its own node:

```sql
EXPLAIN SELECT i FROM rusty_sequence(10000) WHERE i > 9995;
```

```
╭─ Filter ─────────────────╮
│ Expression: i > 9995     │
│ ~2,000 rows              │
╰─────────────┬────────────╯
╭─ Rusty Sequence ─────────╮
│ Function: RUSTY_SEQUENCE │
│ Projections: i           │
│ ~10,000 rows             │
╰──────────────────────────╯
```

## Testing
This extension uses the DuckDB Python client for testing. This should be automatically installed in the `make configure` step.
The tests themselves are written in the SQLLogicTest format, just like most of DuckDB's tests. A sample test can be found in
`test/sql/<extension_name>.test`. To run the tests using the *debug* build:

```shell
make test_debug
```

or for the *release* build:
```shell
make test_release
```

### Version switching
Testing with different DuckDB versions is really simple:

First, run
```
make clean_all
```
to ensure the previous `make configure` step is deleted.

Then, run
```
DUCKDB_TEST_VERSION=v1.3.2 make configure
```
to select a different duckdb version to test with

Finally, build and test with
```
make debug
make test_debug
```

### Known issues
This is a bit of a footgun, but the extensions produced by this template may (or may not) be broken on windows on python3.11
with the following error on extension load:
```shell
IO Error: Extension '<name>.duckdb_extension' could not be loaded: The specified module could not be found
```
This was resolved by using python 3.12

.PHONY: clean clean_all

PROJ_DIR := $(dir $(abspath $(lastword $(MAKEFILE_LIST))))

EXTENSION_NAME=rusty_quack

# Mark the extension as C_STRUCT_UNSTABLE: DuckDB 2.x requires the _init_c_api_v2 entrypoint.
# Binaries load only in the exact TARGET_DUCKDB_VERSION, not in newer DuckDB releases.
USE_UNSTABLE_C_API=1
CAPI_VERSION=2

# Target DuckDB version
TARGET_DUCKDB_VERSION=v2.0.0

all: configure debug

# Include makefiles from DuckDB
include extension-ci-tools/makefiles/c_api_extensions/base.Makefile
include extension-ci-tools/makefiles/c_api_extensions/rust.Makefile

# Build workspace libraries rather than the CI tools' Wasm example target.
IS_EXAMPLE=
ifneq ($(DUCKDB_WASM_PLATFORM),)
	TARGET_INFO=--target $(TARGET) --package rusty_quack_wasm
else
	TARGET_INFO+=--package rusty_quack
endif

configure: venv platform extension_version

debug: build_extension_library_debug build_extension_with_metadata_debug
release: build_extension_library_release build_extension_with_metadata_release

test: test_debug
test_debug: test_extension_debug
test_release: test_extension_release

clean: clean_build clean_rust
clean_all: clean_configure clean

# name: test/sql/rusty_quack.test
# description: Fill all four output vectors from the table callback
# group: [quack]

require rusty_quack

query TTTI
SELECT * FROM rusty_quack(['Alice', NULL, 'Bob', 'Cara']) ORDER BY total_index NULLS LAST;
----
Cara	🐤	Cara|	0
Bob	🦀	Cara|Bob|	1
Alice	🐥	Cara|Bob|Alice|	3
NULL	NULL	NULL	NULL

query I
SELECT count(*) FROM rusty_quack([]::VARCHAR[]);
----
0

query I
SELECT count(*) FROM rusty_quack(NULL::VARCHAR[]);
----
0

# name: test/sql/rusty_longest.test
# description: rusty_longest aggregate: the longest string, ties to the lexicographically smaller one
# group: [quack]

require rusty_quack

# Criterion 3 / candidate T1: the longest non-NULL input wins.
query T
SELECT rusty_longest(s) FROM (VALUES ('a'), ('ccc'), ('bb'), (NULL)) v(s);
----
ccc

# Empty input gives NULL.
query T
SELECT rusty_longest(s) FROM (SELECT 'x'::VARCHAR AS s WHERE false);
----
NULL

# Ties resolve to the lexicographically smaller string, so the result does not depend on input order.
query T
SELECT rusty_longest(s) FROM (VALUES ('zz'), ('aa'), ('mm')) v(s);
----
aa

# name: test/sql/quack_type.test
# description: QUACK custom type and the INTEGER -> QUACK cast
# group: [quack]

require rusty_quack

# Criterion 8 / candidate T4.
query T
SELECT 3::QUACK;
----
quackquackquack

# Out of range: TRY_CAST gives NULL, CAST raises the cast's own error.
query T
SELECT TRY_CAST(11 AS QUACK);
----
NULL

statement error
SELECT CAST(11 AS QUACK);
----
between 0 and 10

# name: test/sql/rusty_echo.test
# description: test rusty_echo scalar function
# group: [quack]

# Before we load the extension, this will fail
statement error
SELECT rusty_echo('x');
----
Catalog Error: Scalar Function with name rusty_echo does not exist!

# Require statement will ensure the extension is loaded from now on
require rusty_quack

# Confirm the extension works
query T
SELECT rusty_echo(col0) FROM values ('Hello'), ('rusty'), ('world') as v;
----
🐤 Hello 🦀 Hello
🐤 rusty 🦀 rusty
🐤 world 🦀 world

# Constant NULL inputs are folded to NULL.
query T
SELECT rusty_echo(NULL);
----
NULL

# Runtime NULLs in regular input chunks must be masked by the scalar function.
query T
SELECT rusty_echo(s) FROM (VALUES (1, 'a'), (2, NULL), (3, 'b')) v(i, s) ORDER BY i;
----
🐤 a 🦀 a
NULL
🐤 b 🦀 b

# Empty string: surface it via length and a hex digest, since trailing
# whitespace in the literal template output is fragile under sqllogictest.
query II
SELECT length(rusty_echo('')), md5(rusty_echo(''));
----
5	07058a80443e7a547044e2a53aea9304

# Non-ASCII inputs round-trip through DuckString.
query T
SELECT rusty_echo(col0) FROM values ('привет'), ('你好') as v;
----
🐤 привет 🦀 привет
🐤 你好 🦀 你好

# Exact signature: wrong arity / wrong type is rejected by the binder.
statement error
SELECT rusty_echo();
----
Binder Error

statement error
SELECT rusty_echo(42);
----
Binder Error

# Inputs spanning multiple DataChunks (STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE = 2048).
query II
SELECT count(*), count(DISTINCT rusty_echo(s::VARCHAR)) FROM range(3000) t(s);
----
3000	3000

# name: test/sql/rusty_sequence.test
# description: rusty_sequence table function: chunked output and filter pushdown
# group: [quack]

require rusty_quack

# Criterion 3 / candidate T2: 5000 rows cross the 2048-row chunk boundary several times.
query II
SELECT count(*), max(i) FROM rusty_sequence(5000);
----
5000	4999

# Criterion 5 / candidate T3: `i < constant` is claimed by the function and the result stays exact.
query I
SELECT count(*) FROM rusty_sequence(5000) WHERE i < 10;
----
10

# Criterion 5 / candidate T3: projecting only `i`. This query cannot observe whether `label`
# was skipped; the projection itself is checked with EXPLAIN in the evidence.
query I
SELECT i FROM rusty_sequence(3) ORDER BY i;
----
0
1
2

# name: test/sql/rusty_docs.test
# description: every function the extension registers is documented in duckdb_functions()
# group: [quack]

require rusty_quack

# Criterion 4 / candidate T9: the functions and their kinds. DISTINCT folds overloads.
query TT
SELECT DISTINCT function_name, function_type
FROM duckdb_functions()
WHERE function_name LIKE 'rusty\_%' ESCAPE '\'
ORDER BY function_name, function_type;
----
rusty_echo	scalar
rusty_longest	aggregate
rusty_quack	table
rusty_sequence	table

# Every function has a description, at least one example, and no auto-generated parameter name.
query I
SELECT count(*)
FROM duckdb_functions()
WHERE function_name LIKE 'rusty\_%' ESCAPE '\'
  AND (
    description IS NULL
    OR coalesce(len(examples), 0) = 0
    OR len(list_filter(parameters, lambda p: regexp_matches(p, '^col[0-9]+$'))) > 0
  );
----
0

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail

usage() {
    echo "Usage: $0 NEO_VERSION MACROS_VERSION (e.g. $0 0.20000.0 1.20000.0)" >&2
    exit 1
}

VERSION_PATTERN='^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)\.([1-9][0-9]{4,})\.(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$'
if [ "$#" -ne 2 ] || [[ ! "$1" =~ $VERSION_PATTERN ]] || [[ ! "$2" =~ $VERSION_PATTERN ]]; then
    usage
fi

NEO_VERSION=$1
MACROS_VERSION=$2
IFS=. read -r _ ENCODED_VERSION _ <<<"$NEO_VERSION"
IFS=. read -r _ MACROS_ENCODED_VERSION _ <<<"$MACROS_VERSION"
if [[ "$ENCODED_VERSION" != "$MACROS_ENCODED_VERSION" ]] || ((ENCODED_VERSION < 20000)); then
    echo "Both crates must target the same DuckDB version (2.0.0 or newer)." >&2
    usage
fi
printf -v API_VERSION '%d.%d.%d' \
    "$((ENCODED_VERSION / 10000))" "$((ENCODED_VERSION / 100 % 100))" "$((ENCODED_VERSION % 100))"
DUCKDB_VERSION=v$API_VERSION

cd "$(dirname "$0")"

sed_inplace() {
    if sed --version 2>/dev/null | grep -q GNU; then
        sed -i "$@"
    else
        sed -i '' "$@"
    fi
}

sed_inplace -E "s!^TARGET_DUCKDB_VERSION=.*!TARGET_DUCKDB_VERSION=$DUCKDB_VERSION!" Makefile
sed_inplace -E "/duckdb_version:/s!v[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+!$DUCKDB_VERSION!g" \
    .github/workflows/MainDistributionPipeline.yml
sed_inplace -E "/^duckdb-neo[[:space:]]*=/s!version = \"[^\"]+\"!version = \"~$NEO_VERSION\"!" Cargo.toml
sed_inplace -E "/^duckdb-loadable-macros[[:space:]]*=/s!version = \"[^\"]+\"!version = \"~$MACROS_VERSION\"!" Cargo.toml
sed_inplace -E "s!api_version = \"[^\"]+\"!api_version = \"$API_VERSION\"!" \
    crates/native/src/lib.rs crates/wasm/src/lib.rs

echo "Updated duckdb-neo to $NEO_VERSION and duckdb-loadable-macros to $MACROS_VERSION / DuckDB $DUCKDB_VERSION"
echo "Note: run cargo update to refresh Cargo.lock; dependencies were not resolved."
echo "Note: update the extension-ci-tools workflow ref, ci_tools_version, and submodule manually."

# statically linking the C runtime on windows seems sensible?
[target.x86_64-pc-windows-msvc]
rustflags = ["-Ctarget-feature=+crt-static"]
